1989-2000.what: Ground-floor front reworked in 1997: the left-hand ground-floor window was filled in with a plain flat panel under a new long fascia board, and the single door became a double door, so the ground floor reads as a shop or garage front. A dark box (sign or light box) sits above it.
1989-2000.why: Looks like a change of use of the ground floor, a shop or store front put in a dwelling front.

1989-2000.what: The upper window on the side (gable) wall was renewed in 1998: it went from a thin plain frame to a larger frame with a projecting sill and a hood over it.
1989-2000.why: Window replaced or renovated by the owner, ordinary upkeep.

1989-2000.what: A stroke is tagged 1993 on E but I could not see anything change on E in any view (at most a very slight darkening of the siding, and that could be my imagination). I am not claiming a change.

2000-2010.what: A two-storey extension was added in 2003 on the lane side of B: a glazed ground floor (many narrow panes on the lane side plus a larger window and door bay) with a balcony with a railing on top, running out toward the lane.
2000-2010.why: Owner built on a glazed room or porch with a balcony; looks like an extension for more living or business space.

2000-2010.what: In 2007 the boards (X-crossed shutters) over D's three front windows came off and ordinary glazed windows with frames appeared, the attic window and the two ground-floor windows. D went from boarded-up to open.
2000-2010.why: The house was brought back into use after standing empty, with the windows repaired or reopened.

2000-2010.what: In 2008 E's windows were boarded up with X-crossed boards: the attic window and both ground-floor windows on the front gable.
2000-2010.why: Looks like the house was left empty or abandoned and shut up.

2010-2020.what: In 2011 C's windows were renewed: the two front windows and the lower side window got new, larger frames with trim around them (they were plainer before).
2010-2020.why: Window replacement or renovation, as part of upkeep or the owner doing the house up.

2010-2020.what: In 2016 A's shopfront was taken out: the big dark shop window and the fascia board above it were replaced by two ordinary house windows with frames, one small at the corner and one larger in the middle, alongside the existing window and door.
2010-2020.why: The shop closed and the ground floor was turned back into a dwelling.

how_well: The tags and the order of strokes made it easy to find where to look, and the changes that are big in the eye-level view (B's extension, A's shopfront, B's front, D's boards) were easy to read, but at street, 12 m and city views the small ones (C's windows, E) were hard to see, and I saw nothing at all for E's 1993 tag. The city view added almost nothing beyond showing where the changes are; the one change I found only in the 12 m view was C's side window, and E's boarding I could only make out by looking very closely.
believed: That a change really happened at every tag; for E in 1993 the tag promised a change that I could not see in any picture.
That the year on the tag is when the change happened; the picture only shows that it was there by then, and the repainting makes it look like something got built or came off in that exact year.
That a tag with only a house letter says what the change was; the 'why' (shop closed, house left empty, owner renovated, new use) is my guess from the look, not something shown.

That the pictures show everything that changed: only changes that face the camera can be seen, so changes on the back, inside, or on roofs would be missed, and many of the small ones are only visible at eye level.
